# Emoji provenance

The reaction picker, the quick reactions and the reaction chips draw
emoji as pictures rather than text. Sailfish's Qt is 5.6, which cannot
draw a colour font, and the system fonts know a few hundred emoji at
most, in monochrome -- the stock keyboard offers thirty. Every other
emoji is an empty box. So Piirit ships a picture per emoji, the way
Fernschreiber does on the same platform, and draws text only for one it
has no picture for (`qml/components/EmojiGlyph.qml`).

Two things are committed, both generated by `scripts/fetch-emoji.py`,
which pins its inputs and refuses anything that does not match:

- `qml/js/EmojiData.js` -- which emoji the picker offers, in Unicode's
  order and groups, with the English name and keywords a search matches.
- `qml/art/emoji/*.png` -- one 72x72 picture for each of them, unmodified.

`--check` fetches both inputs again and requires the committed copies to
match them byte for byte; CI runs that (`ci/vendor-check.sh`).

## Pictures: Twemoji

- **Project:** Twemoji, maintained by jdecked after Twitter stopped
- **Source:** https://github.com/jdecked/twemoji
- **Version / tag:** `v17.0.3`, commit
  `b6b55fef1e8636b540a6d016a4729ca8cdf2e60b`
- **Files:** `assets/72x72/*.png`, the ones `EmojiData.js` names
- **Licence:** the graphics are licensed under
  [CC-BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).
  Copyright (c) 2014-2021 Twitter, Inc and other contributors;
  Copyright (c) 2022-present Jason Sofonia & Justine De Caires.
  The pictures are not changed.

## Data: emojibase-data

- **Project:** Emojibase, by Miles Johnson
- **Source:** https://github.com/milesj/emojibase, published to npm as
  `emojibase-data`
- **Version:** `17.0.0`, tarball sha256
  `d01d0e2ca4e22cb402679532155342c71e2e871f25c32223c013b8b166ebdf5a`
- **Files:** `en/data.json`, of which each emoji's character, group,
  order, name and keywords are kept; skin-tone variants and the
  components group are left out
- **Licence:** MIT, Copyright (c) 2017-2019 Miles Johnson. The names and
  keywords come from the Unicode CLDR annotations, under the
  [Unicode License v3](https://www.unicode.org/license.txt),
  Copyright (c) 1991-2025 Unicode, Inc.

## Updating

Bump `TWEMOJI_TAG` with `TWEMOJI_COMMIT`, or `EMOJIBASE_VERSION` with
`EMOJIBASE_SHA256`, in `scripts/fetch-emoji.py`, run it, and update this
file to match. Keep the two on the same Unicode version: an emoji in the
data with no picture fails the script rather than drawing as a box.
